lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about getting older, about age.
My neighbour Mr Aliyev has a birthday today. Happy birthday, Mr Aliyev!
How old is he? He is a grandfather, right?
Yes. Aysu asked him, "How old are you?" He said, "I'm seventy." Then he laughed. "No, no. I am eighty." And he says, "I'm twenty-one, with sixty years of experience."
[laugh] He is very young. He walks every day. He is slow, but he does not stop.
Yes. He gets up at five. He sits down in the garden. He drinks tea.
His health is good. He is well. My health is not good. I am thirty-two, and I am tired.
You slow down after one cake. He eats three cakes today.
Three? Is that good for his health?
He says, "At eighty, a cake is medicine."
I want to be like Mr Aliyev when I am old.
First, you need to get up at five. Bye for now!

words.en: the father of your mother or father
the day you were born, every year

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is growing older. And a party for a very special man.
Mr Aliyev is eighty today. He retired twenty years ago, and he says it was the busiest time of his life.
He took up gardening, then fishing, and last year he learned to use a smartphone.
He phones me with a photo of his tomatoes every morning. I look after his plants when he travels.
His memory is amazing. He knows every neighbour's birthday. I forget mine. And his health? He never slows down.
Never. He has a lot of experience with life. He says, "Never give up, and never give up tea."
He says age is just a number. And a number can be forgotten.
At the party, a young man asked him, "Mr Aliyev, are you tired?" He said, "A little. I'm only slow in the morning."
[laugh] Slow in the morning. Like me.
How do you feel about getting older, Sam?
Honestly? I'm only afraid of two things: my first wrinkle and my first pension form.
You're only as old as you feel.
Then I'm ninety. See you next time!

words.en: what you know from doing things
a phone that works like a small computer

words.phrase: You're only as old as you feel.
words.az: Özünü neçə yaşda hiss edirsənsə, o qədərsən.
words.tr: İnsan kendini kaç yaşında hissediyorsa o yaştadır.
words.en: your real age is how young you feel

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is getting older, and what the older people around us teach us.
Mr Aliyev is eighty, and he's the most active person on our street. He keeps up with everyone, even the teenagers.
He has a simple rule: don't slow down just because the calendar says so.
When I look at him, I think wisdom isn't about age, it's about attention. He remembers the names of my parents' friends, and what they ordered at my sister's wedding.
In England, many older people live in care homes. It isn't always lonely, but it's a different idea of independence.
Here, three generations usually live under one roof. It can be noisy, but nobody feels left out.
Last month Mr Aliyev looked back on his life at a family dinner. He said, "I was never rich, but I was always busy, and that's better."
That is the secret. People who stay active are happier, even if their knees say no.
I hope I'm young at heart like him. Though I'll need a better excuse than "my knee."
A question for our listeners: who is the oldest person you know, and what do they teach you?
Mine is Mr Aliyev. And he taught me how to peel a pomegranate. See you next time!

words.en: people born around the same time
think about something in your past
move or change as fast as others
old in years but young in spirit
getting better as it gets older
